facts.statement: Zhyrasuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph known only from fragmentary fossils, including a frontal bone from the roof of the skull.
facts.quote: Zhyrasuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of crocodylomorph that may have been a crocodylid eusuchian, but is only known from scanty material including a frontal (one of the bones of the roof of the skull).

facts.statement: The genus Zhyrasuchus was described in 1989 by Lev Nessov and colleagues.
facts.quote: Zhyrasuchus was described in 1989 by Lev Nessov and colleagues.

facts.statement: Fossils of Zhyrasuchus were found in the Coniacian-age Upper Cretaceous Bissekty Formation in Dzharakhuduk, Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in the Coniacian-age Upper Cretaceous Bissekty Formation of Dzharakhuduk, Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: Zhyrasuchus is classified within the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
Zhyrasuchus is tentatively classified in the family Crocodylidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Zhyrasuchus as Crocodylidae.

A 2000 review by Glenn Storrs and Mikhail Efimov could not determine the relationship between Zhyrasuchus and the contemporary Tadzhikosuchus, or if they were synonyms, due to the scarcity of fossil material.
facts.quote: A 2000 review by Glenn Storrs and Mikhail Efimov could not determine how Zhyrasuchus and the contemporaneous Tadzhikosuchus were related, or even if they were synonyms, due to the poor fossils available.

facts.statement: Zhyrasuchus lived during the Turonian stage of the Cretaceous, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)
